summary: 1932 68-foot steel lookout on Borden Mountain in Savoy Mountain State Forest; earlier stations on Tower Mountain; a 2024 hiking write-up calls it fenced off.

facts.design: 68-foot steel tower with 10 by 10 foot wooden cab
facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

access.note: A 2024 hiking write-up describes the tower as fenced off; no official access statement was found

visit.trail_note: A 2024 hiking write-up says the easiest access is via a paved road; the tower itself is fenced off

events.note: Tree-top station, built to supplement Mount Greylock per NHLR; FFLOS places a 1913 platform in a tree on Tower Mountain
35-foot wooden tower on Tower Mountain used through 1915 (FFLOS)
Tower Mountain site abandoned at end of 1915 season; primary Savoy site switched to Borden Mountain
Present 68-foot steel tower with 10 by 10 foot wooden cab went into service
Observer Ernest Peabody, on duty daily from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (North Adams Transcript, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Lightning damaged the tower and telephone and power lines; observer Theodore S. Brown was on forced leave
Ordered reopened April 11, 1955 as fire danger rose, by State District Fire Warden Francis Mahoney
Registered December 15, 2004 as US 624, MA 35; nominated by Henry Isenberg
FFLOS US 52, MA 52 covers the former Tower Mountain site, not the standing tower

corrections.current: FFLOS US 52 (savoy-tower-site) listed as a registration of this tower
corrections.proposed: Keep FFLOS US 52 as a separate former-site record for the 1913-1915 Tower Mountain station; it does not describe the standing Borden Mountain tower
corrections.why: The FFLOS page is titled Savoy Tower Site, gives a 2,370 ft Tower Mountain location, and has coordinates that differ from the NHLR coordinates for the standing tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR describes a 45-foot steel tower with an 8 by 8 foot cab and gives no date. The FFLOS page gives a 35-foot wooden tower built in 1914 on Tower Mountain. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Build history rests on the NHLR and the Forest Lookouts newspaper transcriptions, which agree on 1932. Current standing and public access rest on a 2024 hiking write-up and an undated Wikipedia summary; no official 2025-2026 source was read. A search snippet from the Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts chapter (not opened) says the 1932 tower replaced a shorter iron tower from 1915, which conflicts with the 1914 wooden tower. Worth checking if that page can be opened.
